"The legend begins... with Pam."

A new Crystal Lake trailer has dropped to remind you that the original Friday the 13th killer wasn't Jason Voorhees. It was his mother, Pamela Voorhees. 

A24's highly anticipated Crystal Lake TV show is making a major stop at New York Comic Con before its official debut on Peacock and HBO Max. The studio has confirmed that the Crystal Lake premiere episode will receive an exclusive first-look screening at the Empire Stage at the Javits Center in New York City.

Following the screening, attendees will be treated to a panel discussion featuring series creator Brad Caleb Kane (IT Welcome to Derry) and several members of the cast, including Linda Cardellini (Pamela), William Catlett, Devin Kessler, Cameron Scoggins (Officer Dorf), Gwendolyn Sundstrom (Claudette), and Callum Vinson (Jason). 

This early screening offers a unique opportunity for fans to see how the production expands the mythology of the Friday the 13th franchise. By showcasing the episode at a major event like New York Comic Con, the creative team is signaling confidence in the Crystal Lake series as it prepares for its wider streaming release.

Serving as a Friday the 13th prequel series to the 1980 horror movie classic, Crystal Lake trailer focuses on the life of Pamela Voorhees before she became the iconic killer. Linda Cardellini stars as Pamela, portraying a single mother struggling with grief nearly a year after the tragic drowning of her young son, Jason Voorhees. The narrative kicks off when two strangers arrive at her home to investigate her past, triggering a disturbing chain of events.

While the premise leans into psychological drama and conspiracy thriller elements, creator Kane has assured fans that the horror series will eventually embrace the bloody horror associated with the iconic horror movie franchise. He has teased that the series will feature numerous connections to the original films, including various Viernes 13 Easter eggs and recreations of familiar elements that long-time Friday the 13th fans will recognize.

The Camp Crystal Lake horror series has seen significant changes since it was first ordered by Peacock in 2022. While Bryan Fuller was initially attached as the writer and show runner, he departed the A24 project in 2024, leading to Kane taking over creative duties. Despite these behind-the-scenes shifts, the crystal lake show has already secured distribution with HBO Max for Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the UK, and Ireland.

All eight episodes of Crystal Lake premiere on Peacock October 15, 2026 and internationally on HBO Max by year's end.

snippet.description:
What Happens When Joe Satriani Joins Mick Jagger? | “Start Me Up” Live 1988

Filmed live at the Tokyo Dome in Japan, this historic concert captures Mick Jagger operating at the absolute peak of his stage energy. Backed by a phenomenal solo tour supergroup—featuring guitar hero Joe Satriani and legendary drummer Simon Phillips—Jagger electrifies over 50,000 fans with non-stop swagger and crowd-commanding charisma.

🚀 The Live Lineup:

🎤 Mick Jagger – Lead Vocals
🎸 Joe Satriani – Lead Guitar
🎸 Jimmy Rip – Guitar
🎸 Doug Wimbish – Bass Guitar
🥁 Simon Phillips – Drums
🎹 Phil Ashley – Keyboards
🎤 Syreeta Wright & Carol Kenyon – Backing Vocals

📋 5 Fast Facts About the Performance & Liner Notes:

• *The 1981 "Tattoo You" Anthem* – Originally released in August 1981 as the lead single for The Rolling Stones' album *Tattoo You*, "Start Me Up" reached #2 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and became the defining stadium opener for the band's 1980s era.
• *The Long-Awaited Japanese Debut* – Due to Japanese visa restrictions that blocked 1970s and 1981 tour dates, Jagger's solo performances at the Tokyo Dome marked the very first time Japanese audiences got to hear these 1981 Stones classics performed live by their original lead singer.
• *Virtuoso Guitar Support* – Fresh off his breakout instrumental solo album *Surfing with the Alien*, guitar hero Joe Satriani joined Jagger's touring lineup, bringing signature technical brilliance to Keith Richards' iconic 1981 open-G riff.
• *From Reggae to Rock* – The track originally evolved during the 1978 *Some Girls* sessions as a slow reggae jam named "Never Stop" before being rediscovered and re-recorded into a driving 1981 rock masterpiece.
• *Restored Vault Audio* – Sourced directly from original multi-track broadcast soundboard masters, this high-definition audio restoration isolates Jagger's vocals and Satriani's soaring solos in pristine clarity.
